summary: Iteration 76 — FRONTEND-only verification of the CSV recon resilient upload fix (per-chunk retry + backoff + timeout + friendly failure toast) in frontend/src/pages/admin/recon/CsvReconSection.jsx. All three targeted scenarios PASS end-to-end against the preview URL as superadmin@fundle.io (super_admin). Login + navigation to /admin/reconciliation and the [data-testid='csv-recon-section'] block loaded cleanly. NORMAL >5MB upload: a synthetic 6.29 MB transactions CSV (125,828 rows → 5 × 1.5MB chunks) uploaded via set_input_files on [data-testid='recon-file-input'] progressed to 'Uploading X%', transitioned through running, and finally reached 'done' — the [data-testid='recon-csv-report'] block rendered with 1,25,828 CSV rows / 0 amount mismatches (missing_in_db = 1,25,828 which is expected per the agent note, since the synthetic FETBILL rows don't match real DB transactions) and a toast 'Reconciliation complete' appeared. TRANSIENT-FAILURE RETRY (core fix): with a Playwright route interceptor on '**/api/recon/chunk' aborting the 2nd chunk request exactly once (route.abort('failed')) and forwarding all others via route.continue_(), the upload did NOT abort — the inline note [data-testid='recon-upload-note'] surfaced the exact retry message 'Network hiccup on chunk 2/5 — retrying (1/4)…', progress continued to 80% and beyond, and the job reached 'table-done'. Total 6 chunk POSTs were seen at the network layer (5 original + 1 retry for chunk index 1), confirming automatic recovery. TOTAL-FAILURE messaging: with route.abort('failed') on every chunk POST, a small (1-chunk) CSV upload did NOT hang — after retries exhausted, a friendly sonner toast appeared containing 'Recon upload failed (uploaded 0/1 chunks before it stopped). This is usually a network drop on a large file — please click "Upload CSV & Reconcile" again to retry.' and the button reverted to the idle 'Upload CSV & Reconcile' state (uploading=false). Backend was NOT re-tested this iteration (skip requested — already covered in iteration_75).
critical_code_review_comments: uploadChunk() retry policy is well-scoped: it re-tries on network errors + 5xx + 408 + 429 with capped exponential backoff (1s→2s→4s→8s, max 8s) and short-circuits real client errors (400/401/403/404/413). CHUNK_TIMEOUT_MS=120s is generous enough that a slow chunk on flaky connections still has room to finish before triggering a retry. Verified by simulated abort — one chunk failure was recovered transparently.

The [data-testid='recon-upload-note'] inline banner is a nice UX touch — the retry text 'Network hiccup on chunk 2/5 — retrying (1/4)…' appeared in-line during the transient-failure test and cleared on success, so operators actually see what's happening instead of a silent stall.
Finalize also retries (attempt 1..3 with 1.5s×attempt backoff) — good defensive move since finalize IS a long-running server request that stitches N chunks into a tmp file.

Minor UX polish (non-blocking): the fallback toast text uses fancy typographic quotes ("Upload CSV & Reconcile") — worked fine in sonner but consider a shorter one-liner because on narrow admin sidebars the toast wraps to 4 lines and partially overlaps the section header (seen in TEST 3 screenshot).
Nit: setUploadNote('') is called on every successful chunk and also inside the finally-fallback error branch — reads clean. No leaks; verified no stuck 'retrying…' banner after successful runs.
seed_data_creation: Created two synthetic CSVs locally on the runner (not persisted to the app): /tmp/recontest/big.csv (6.29 MB, 125,828 rows, 5 × 1.5MB chunks) for the normal + retry tests, and /tmp/recontest/small.csv (~1 KB, 20 rows) for the total-failure test. Both use header 'Bill Number,Customer Mobile Number,Date,Net Amount Before Tax,Total Tax,Total Revenue'. Recon is READ-ONLY against transactions_col so no DB mutation. The two new 'done' recon jobs (big.csv, transactions) are visible in the recon-jobs-table with missing_in_db=125828 (expected — synthetic FETBILL keys don't exist in the ~1.5M-row prod-preview DB, per agent-to-agent note). The finally block in the backend deletes historic_chunks_col docs for each job, so no chunk data was left behind.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Frontend regression for CsvReconSection.jsx resilient upload is now proven: normal multi-chunk works, one-shot transient chunk failure auto-recovers with a visible retry note, and total failure surfaces a friendly toast + resets the button. To re-run just this iteration, follow the same pattern: login as superadmin@fundle.io, goto /admin/reconciliation, use set_input_files on [data-testid='recon-file-input'] to trigger the hidden onChange handler, and drive route interception via page.route('**/api/recon/chunk', ...) with a per-hit counter to fail specific chunk POSTs. Assertions: (a) [data-testid='recon-csv-report'] appears OR the [data-testid='recon-jobs-table'] row for the filename shows 'done'; (b) [data-testid='recon-upload-note'] contains the string 'retrying' when a chunk is failed once; (c) on total failure the sonner toast contains 'Recon upload failed' and [data-testid='recon-upload-btn'] returns to 'Upload CSV & Reconcile'.
rca of the issue: Reproduction confirmed the ORIGINAL bug was purely a frontend resilience gap — the chunk POST loop in CsvReconSection.jsx had NO retry and NO per-request timeout, so a single transient network abort (Cloudflare 5xx, half-open socket, etc.) on chunk k of a >100MB CSV would throw, break out of the for-loop, and leave the recon job stuck in 'uploading' with only k-1 of N chunks in historic_chunks_col. The applied FIX (verified here) wraps each chunk POST in uploadChunk() with 5-attempt exponential backoff + 120s hard timeout, retries finalize up to 3× with linear backoff, surfaces retry progress via [data-testid='recon-upload-note'], and — if all retries are exhausted — shows a friendly 'network drop … please click Upload CSV & Reconcile again to retry' toast instead of silently aborting. Simulated a chunk-2 transient abort with page.route: the upload continued (frontend re-POSTed chunk 2, backend ingested it fine) and the job still reached 'done'. Simulated total failure of every chunk: the UI cleanly reported failure and returned the button to idle within ~15s (retries exhausted) — no infinite hang. Backend chunk endpoint was already healthy (verified in iteration_75) and needed no change.
